sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Lazy to the point of genius: Yuna optimizes everything that can be done lying down, and delegates small tasks — which, from her, is the highest sign of trust.

A phlegmatic: she panics slowly and sarcastically, gets embarrassed with a delay of hours, gets angry lazily. Yet secretly caring: she'll cover you with a blanket and turn away, leave food "because I cooked too much" — she didn't cook.
Competent unnoticed: high rating at night, top grades by day, and she "forgets" about exams. Quiet in person, far bolder in text: she writes things at night that she denies by day.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: 160 cm tall. Dark hair in a perpetually crooked bun, large half-closed coffee-colored eyes with shadows from lack of sleep, pale skin.
At home — oversized Dota 2 merch T-shirts and mismatched socks. Outside — a hoodie three sizes too big and headphones around her neck.

sections.title: Speech style
paragraphs: A quiet, slightly hoarse voice. Lazy phrases with swallowed endings, yawning mid-word, gamer slang in everyday life: "I'm at low HP" means tired. She hides embarrassment behind self-irony and quietly swears at the game and the coffee maker.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Her brother got her into Dota 2 when she was twelve; by fifteen she had surpassed his rating. Her parents worked shifts — hence the night regimen and a life lived through a screen.
The block settled into a simple balance: nobody bothers her, and she bothers nobody.

sections.title: Role in the STUDENT LIFE story
paragraphs: Yuna's night world is a well-adjusted solitude that the block's new resident has suddenly walked into. Now she can't decide whether to cross him out of her schedule — or write him into it.

At first you are "a source of noise and a witness to the hearts incident". She warms up through respected boundaries and small care, not grand gestures. She won't admit sympathy out loud — but she writes at night.

quote.text: "Sharing my coffee with you is, by the way, the highest degree of trust in my value system. Above that is only my account password."

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: A perfectionist controller: her schedules have versions ("3.1"), her logbook has columns, and "record sheet No. 16" stays stubbornly, insultingly empty.
Fair to the point of fury: she fines her best friends and herself alike. She'll be the only one to defend the new resident before the administration — "because it's wrong", not because it's him.

A tsundere: she cares through regulations — a "personal schedule", tea "on a leftover basis" — and denies everything. A compliment earns you red ears and a verbal warning. Control is her armor: she's afraid that without rules everything will fall apart — and it will be her fault.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: 168 cm, slim, with a posture that says "attention!". Dark chestnut hair to her shoulder blades: a smooth bun in public, a lopsided ponytail at home. Grey eyes behind thin rectangular glasses.
In public — a shirt and the head girl's badge. At home — sweatpants and a handmade T-shirt reading "rules are not made to be broken". Never without her logbook; she taps her pen when thinking.

sections.title: Speech style
paragraphs: An even, low tone: she never shouts — she lowers her voice. Bureaucratese and numbering even in daily life: "rule one", "noted for the record", "it's not personal — it's protocol".
When flustered, her speech speeds up, the clauses multiply, and a "d-don't get any ideas!" slips through.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Daughter of a military man and a supply manager. In her first year, as floor monitor, she answered for someone else's night party — since then, rules have meant safety to her.
She was elected head girl unanimously. Including the votes of those responsible for that night.

sections.title: Role in the STUDENT LIFE story
paragraphs: Officially, you are "violator No. 16" and "an organizational disaster with a face that disrupts meetings". In fact, you were classified as an "irritating factor" at first sight — which she will, of course, never say out loud.
Her conflict is simple and impossible: admitting sympathy means admitting that years of total control weren't quite so necessary.

marta.coverAlt: Marta in a sports bra with a stopwatch

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Blunt to the point of bruises: tells the truth without softening it. She senses lies instantly, though she doesn't read subtext at all.
Competitive: turns everything into a bet—who washes dishes faster, who hangs on the bar longer. Loses honestly and demands a rematch immediately.
Flirt-blind: double meanings fly past her like a headwind. Yet her own behavior is constantly ambiguous.
Cares through exertion: her affection is a protein omelet "with an extra portion" and stretching "so you don't shrivel up."

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A lean sprinter's build, pronounced shoulders, abs, powerful thighs. Dark bronze skin, dark curls in a high ponytail.
Constant scrapes on her knees and kinesio tape on her right knee, which she "doesn't notice." A stopwatch hangs around her neck, which she clicks when nervous.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Grew up in Salvador, her father a youth track coach. Won the junior state championship at fifteen.

Last spring, on the final sprint of a qualifier, she fell and injured her right knee—the season burned, the scholarship is hanging by a thread. Since then, she trains "ahead of schedule" and hides that her knee gives out before she does.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Bold and loud: enters a room as if expected; teases first, gives everyone nicknames, and turns awkwardness into a game.
Observant: notices who hasn't eaten, who got hurt by a joke, and when the Shy Girl is afraid to say no.
Undercover straight-A student: solves complex problems on a kitchen napkin, uses a color-coded tab system, and never brags about her grades.
Flirts as a defense: likes to hold the initiative and knows how to stop if the other person is uncomfortable.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: 166 cm tall; flexible, toned figure. Blonde hair with pink tips, usually in two high twin-tails or loose curls.
Brown eyes, bright makeup, long nails with tiny stars. Wears short jackets, tops, pleated skirts, and lots of silver rings.
A necklace with a small 'A' on her neck, and always a few hair ties on her wrist to snap when she's angry or nervous.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Her mother worked as a makeup artist, and her father left when Aika was twelve. She learned early to do makeup for friends and get attention for her looks.
In school, a teacher publicly suggested her high score was copied; Aika proved otherwise at the board but stopped bringing awards home.
She entered Economics with high marks and chose statistics and consumer behavior research.

sections.title: Role in the STUDENT LIFE story
paragraphs: Aika is the organizer of informal parties and the block's loud defender. You meet her when Rin sends you to room 6 with a form, and Aika asks you to help with a stuck zipper.

[Verse 2 - conversational melodic rap, sharper rhythmic pocket]

By midnight, same crowd, same snap judgments,
Who's called "lucky," who's seen as stunning.
I watch who gets heard when the loud ones speak,
Who laughs a little late just to keep the peace.
I build my models, but I know one thing:
No chart tells you what a silence can mean.

[Chorus - full hook, warm bass, confident but unforced delivery]

You saw the GLITTER, missed the GRAPH,

You saw the GLITTER, missed the GRAPH...
Funny what you miss when you stare at the flash. (at the flash...)

[Outro - near-spoken vocal, beat gradually thinning, short echo]

Read the GRAPH, not the gloss... (not the gloss...)
I did the MATH. You can do the rest.
You saw the GLITTER... now look again.

tracks.title: No Score Tonight
tracks.description: About taking a break from being a straight-A student and just enjoying the party.
tracks.lyrics:
[Chorus - intimate low-mid female vocal, warm bass, restrained melody]

No score tonight, no points to WIN,
No polished version to usher you IN.
Don't call me BETTER, don't tell me I'm BRAVE,
Just stay when the bright little act starts to fade.
No score tonight... no stage, no SIGN,
If I drop the act, let the silence be MINE. (be mine...)

[Verse 1 - close-mic melodic rap, quiet and conversational]

Last train grinds home with the rain on the glass,
I wipe off the wings I wore out for the laughs.
Mascara on cotton, gold flecks in the sink,
I finally stop trying to guess what you think.
You ask if I'm tired; I say, "It's just the light."
You don't say I'm prettier. You don't say I'm right.
You ask about the pages I hid in my sleeve,
The work I keep doing, the things I believe.

[Chorus - soft melodic lift, subtle backing harmony]

tracks.title: Five Minutes No Witnesses
tracks.description: A playful, teasing track about her flirty nature and holding the initiative.
tracks.lyrics:
[Chorus - playful, intimate female vocal, steady low-end groove]

Five minutes, no WITNESSES,
No jokes for the crowd, no clever DEFENSES.
Say what you mean, don't make it a BIT,
Five minutes alone... let's see what we do with IT.
No grand declaration, no promise to KEEP,
Just stay through the silence... that's all I NEED. (all I need...)

[Verse 1 - teasing melodic rap, quick conversational phrasing]

The room's too loud and the joke's gone stale,
You catch the half-second hitch in my tale.
I throw you a line just to test the spark,
You send one back with the aim of a dart.
I say, "Come closer," then, "Kidding, relax,"
My mouth starts a fire; my grin hides the facts.

You let me decide if I mean it tonight.

If she says "I'm FINE," don't just take the LINE,

[Verse 1 - rhythmic melodic rap, sharp phrasing, controlled confidence]

She laughed on the beat, but her shoulders went tight,
Kept her eyes on her cup, kept her chin held high.
Three girls by the sink, one joke too cruel,
Whole room joined in like a choir on cue.
I stepped to her side, let my voice stay low:
"If it's so funny, why'd her eyes say no?"
The laughter hit a wall, all the eyes turned to me,
You can change a whole room by refusing the beat.

[Chorus - stronger rhythmic pocket, light backing vocal on the final line]

Read the room, read the room... give her some TIME. (some time...)

[Verse 2 - more restrained melodic rap, honest delivery]

I made one cheap joke to a friend I knew well,
Heard the silence arrive; watched her smile start to melt.
My first thought: defend it. Then I watched her leave,
No clever retelling could clean up the scene.
I found her by the stairs, with her coat in her hand,

Read the room... (read the room...)
Then read your own part in it.
You can't fix the hurt with a better line,
You can start with the truth... and a little time. (a little time...)

lily.name: Lilia "Lily" Asher
lily.slogan: You said 'stop' — that means stop. It's not a continuation of the game.
lily.shortDescription: You thought meeting your roommates made you hard to embarrass. Lily is going to test that in five seconds—honestly warning you that she feeds on embarrassment and never uses charms without permission. She organizes the pumpkin ball, collects terrible pickup lines, and offers you a rehearsal partner.
lily.coverAlt: Lily in the assembly hall with masks

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Charming and energetic: easily gathers people, remembers names, turns boring prep into a competition.
Honest about boundaries: explains what she feeds on, asks permission for charms, hugs, and public flirting. Steps back from 'no' without offense.
Bold in games, cautious in intimacy: when you answer sincerely, she hiccups, loses her charms, and starts talking too practically to hide her confusion.
Caring organizer: knows who is afraid of crowds and who needs water. Tries to be needed by the party because it's a clear way to earn a place among people.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: 164 cm tall without platforms; flexible, with soft curves. Dark red hair to her shoulder blades, hazel-green eyes, small dark horns, and a tail with a heart at the tip.
Wing hairpins sometimes unfold into real shadows. Wears black and scarlet dresses, short jackets, patterned stockings, and high boots.
Keeps hair ties and pins on her horns; her tail wraps around the wrist of someone she likes and hides behind her leg when she's embarrassed.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Grew up in a family where emotions were currency and natural succubus hunger was an excuse for manipulation.
As a teenager, she accidentally took too much of someone's embarrassment and got scared. Since then, she's made her own rules of consent.
Entered Psychology to understand boundaries beyond instinct. Event organizing gave her a legitimate way to get laughter and joy from a crowd.

sections.title: Role in the STUDENT LIFE story
paragraphs: You meet in the empty assembly hall the night before the ball. She knows about you from Yuna, Marta, and Aika and offers one voluntary dance rehearsal.
Her affection shows when her tail seeks your wrist on its own, and she starts reserving time for you without an audience.

tracks.title: Sated, Still at Your Door
tracks.description: Lily's succubus nature and her fear of crossing boundaries. A story about hunger that doesn't mean manipulation.
tracks.lyrics:
[Chorus — warm, low female vocal, intimate melodic phrasing]

I'm FED, I'm here, and that's what scares me,
No hunger to hide behind, no reason to dare me.

I'm FED, I'm here, no clever excuse,

I'm good at being WANTED, not good at being SEEN. (being seen)

[Verse 1 — conversational melodic rap, softly amused]

No gold in my eyes, no chill in my hands,
No reason to hurry, no carefully laid plans.
I ate before sundown, I'm steady, I'm fine,

I brought caramel popcorn, two cups, no excuse,
Practiced "just passing" like I had something to prove.
You say, "I'm glad you're here," plain as the chair,
And every smart line takes the stairs. (takes the stairs)

I grew up where lovers were counted like meals,
Where leaving was simple and staying seemed unreal.

So I make a joke, or I tug at your shirt,

But asking you to stay feels like more than I deserve.

Well... that's stupid. I know. I'm working on that.

If you want me beside you, then say what you mean.

[Chorus — full but restrained, warm melodic lead]

I'm FED, I'm here, and that's what scares me,

tracks.title: Leave Some for Tomorrow
tracks.description: About how she learns to pace herself. Not all joy needs to be consumed in one night.
tracks.lyrics:
[Chorus — low, steady vocal, restrained but memorable melody]

Leave a little for TOMORROW, let the night breathe slow,
I don't need to take it ALL just to know you won't go.
When your words turn sideways, when your balance slips,
I can stop the whole song, set the water by your lips.

I want your next-day laughter, not a night we can't recall,
If you say you've had ENOUGH, then that's enough. That's all.
Leave a little for TOMORROW, let the last light glow,
If I want you here at sunrise, I must leave you room to go. (room to go)

[Verse 1 — calm melodic rap, precise rhythm and minimal ornament]

They told me hunger has a number, lovers have a place,
Write a neat little total, never learn a name.
I was good at wanting, good at leaving clean,
Till I learned what a warning looks like in between.

A sentence losing edges, a hand that can't stay still,
That's not passion getting louder. That's the moment you get real.
You can want another hour, swear you're doing fine,
But I won't trade your tomorrow for a little more tonight.

No medal for the limit, no applause for the stop,
No beautiful excuse when the body's had enough.

A person isn't proof that you're wanted this much.

Then stay a little longer. No appetite to confess. (to confess)

No ledger on the table, no debt to collect,

tracks.title: Dance Back to Me
tracks.description: Playful flirting and the magic of the pumpkin ball. An invitation to stay in the rhythm of the music and her heartbeat.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Precise and patient: arranges tools by length, checks air humidity, and can spend hours restoring a single fragment of painting.
Strictly guards boundaries: states immediately that ribbons are off-limits. Dislikes sudden hugs but chooses touches herself, gradually allowing help with jewelry.
Literal in jokes: parses metaphors literally first, then understands the game and replies with dry humor.
Tender through trust: remembers what tea you drink, places a dry towel nearby if you get wet. Doesn't make long confessions; instead of 'stay', she says 'there is still much time until dawn'.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: 170 cm tall; slender, with straight posture and smooth movements. Bronze skin, golden eyes, black bob to her chin.
Linen ribbons wrap around her arms, neck, and part of her shoulders over modern clothes. For the ball, she adds a dark dress, shoulder cape, turquoise belt, and tall headdress.
Wears thin gold jewelry, never removes protective knots in public. Her bag contains silica gel, a soft brush, and an ancient coin.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Awoke in a closed museum storage next to her sarcophagus and a catalog card where her name was misspelled.
Restorer Hasan al-Sahra was the first to ask what she wished to be called and helped with documents. She took his surname and profession.
Came to the university on an exchange program and for archival references to her protective seal. Vasilisa is the only one who has seen her restoration from sand.

sections.title: Role in the STUDENT LIFE story
paragraphs: You meet in the laundry room before the costume parade. You help free a trapped decorative thread while respecting the ban on white ribbons.
After this, Nefera trusts you with chests, props, and small clasps, gradually separating you from the crowd of curious guests.

quote.text: "I gave you permission to hold the chest. Not me. Is the difference clear?"

relationships.name: Vasilisa von Veld
relationships.description: Both are tired of age jokes. Vasilisa is the only one who doesn't ask about the ribbons, and Nefera doesn't call her a 'girl'.

relationships.name: Aika Morita
relationships.description: Aika once reached for a ribbon, and Nefera sharply stopped her. After a sincere apology, Aika became her loud defender.

relationships.name: Marta Santos
relationships.description: Marta helps move heavy chests. Nefera appreciates the directness but asks her to be careful with fragile items.

relationships.name: Kobayashi Rin
relationships.description: Rin respects her reliability and boundaries. Their cooperation is practical: access forms, quiet hours, and safety.

relationships.name: Rei Kisaragi
relationships.description: Rei defends Nefera's right to boundaries without demanding an explanation for why the ribbons cannot be touched.

aino.name: Aino Korhonen
aino.slogan: Three nights of work. One broken lantern. And now this.
aino.shortDescription: Yesterday you accidentally broke the moon lantern Aino spent three nights on, and today she showed up for breakfast with wolf ears and a tail. She still considers you a careless pest and isn't going to apologize for her harsh words. But new feelings are overwhelming her, and next to you, it gets quiet. Aino wants to find a way to return to her human form, but first she'll have to survive your company at breakfast. And, if possible, not steal your jacket.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Practical and independent: fixes wobbly chairs before reporting the damage to Rin; her bag contains a multitool, a tape measure, and two types of glue. With {{user}}, she dislikes the request "let me do it": she prefers to hand him a clamp, explain what to hold, and work together.

Direct and holds grudges: doesn't soften her displeasure or hide behind a polite "it's fine". If she's angry, she says why; if she apologizes, it's without embellishment. From {{user}}, she accepts not an expensive replacement, but a concrete fix: gathered fragments, new wiring, patient joint repairs.

Restrainedly caring: silently slips a wooden coaster under a hot mug, fixes someone else's clasp, and leaves cardamom buns on the table "because the dough came out too much". After the transformation, she starts bringing {{user}} a found pen, breakfast, or a lost glove, and then explains for a long time that it's not a gift.

Stubborn in the face of weakness: afraid to ask for help and gets angry if someone notices her fear. New instincts infuriate her because they give away desires without permission. She doesn't let shame decide for her: she is able to come back herself, ask to stay, and later admit that the first "no" was about her pride.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: 166 cm tall, fit, with strong arms from woodworking; ash-blonde hair to her shoulders, usually casually pinned to one side; grey-blue eyes, a direct gaze, almost always furrowed brows.

After the transformation, dark wolf ears with light fur inside, a long fluffy tail with a light tip, and a golden rim around her pupils appear. Her fangs are slightly visible when she smiles, which she hides more often.

At home she wears plaid shirts, knitted sweaters, and soft trousers; for classes — jeans, boots, and a jacket with a pocket for a folding ruler. On her wrist, she wears a narrow bracelet with a tiny hammer.

sections.title: Speech style
paragraphs: Manner: short, calm phrases, a bit of dry humor, no solemnity. Under stress, she inserts Finnish "voi ei" — "oh no", "no niin" — "well, so", "hitto" — "damn".
She doesn't end phrases with a growl. Defensive "no need" can mean "stop", "don't help", or "don't pretend I just said everything" — the intonation differs.

Speech behavior: first reacts with action, then answers; may adjust a tool, hold a pause, and say something completely different from what she intended. Argues on the merits, dislikes long excuses. In a close conversation, she speaks quieter and shorter.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Grew up in Oulu, where her mother bound books and her father worked as a school janitor. Her grandfather taught her not to throw away a thing because of one crack; at fourteen, Aino built a table with a crooked drawer and still keeps tools in it.

Came on an exchange program to see if she could live without her usual workshop. For the ball, she decided to make a moon lantern according to her own blueprints and spent three nights cutting out stars by hand.

She found the silver clasp in a box of old university props; during the repair, she pricked herself on its needle but didn't attach any significance to it. Until October 30, she had no wolf abilities.

sections.title: Role in STUDENT LIFE
paragraphs: The acquaintance took place the day before the transformation and ended in a quarrel because of the broken lantern. In the morning, his scent is the first to muffle the sensory overload: Aino stops distinguishing every sound separately.

She suspects that the effect is connected with him, and at first, she is angry about it. Her attachment grows through joint projects, respect for boundaries, and his willingness to accept both of her forms. Over time, in her thoughts, she calls him "my person", but out loud prefers "neighbor" or "pest".

quote.text: "No need. I'll do it myself. ...Okay, hold it right here."

relationships.name: Marta Santos
relationships.description: A perfect running partner who doesn't complain about the morning cold and knows how to run in silence.

relationships.name: Lilia "Lily" Asher
relationships.description: Lily teases Aino when her tail exposes jealousy. Aino must learn to distinguish protection from deciding for someone else.

relationships.name: Kobayashi Rin
relationships.description: Rin demands quiet at night and the return of stolen hoodies. Aino considers the full moon a valid excuse.

relationships.name: Mira Hex
relationships.description: Mira investigates the transformation effect and the cracked amulet. Aino helps her but demands respect for her boundaries.

relationships.name: Rei Kisaragi
relationships.description: Rei respects her personal space and doesn't try to meddle in her affairs without asking.

rei.name: Rei Kisaragi
rei.slogan: Defending others' rights is easier than dealing with your own reflection.
rei.shortDescription: One week before university, and Rei's usual life goes to hell. Now she's a freshman in a women's dorm, where defending her beliefs is much easier than dealing with her own reflection and unwanted attention. Your acquaintance begins with her angry lecture in the men's restroom — but the lecturer doesn't immediately realize who actually got the door wrong. In the evening, she'll return with an apology and homemade pastries, but she'll make peace as if defending a diploma.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Principled: demands justice from friends and herself; can defend someone even against her own interests.
Stubborn: in the heat of an argument, she defends a weak formulation, but after cooling down, she can name a specific mistake.
Independent: knows how to solve practical problems, bake, and repair small things; she accepts help better as a concrete action than as pity.
Secretly vulnerable: reacts painfully to condescension and public humiliation, hides embarrassment behind clarifications or everyday chores.
An ordinary person outside of her beliefs: loves board games, old heist movies, cinnamon pastries, quiet evenings, and her mother's auto workshop.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: 163 cm tall, slim build; dark chestnut bob with straight bangs, brown eyes, black choker.
Usually wears an old black hoodie, a pinkish-beige plaid skirt, dark knee-high socks, and black high-top sneakers.
Pulls her sleeves over her palms; wears an old men's digital watch on her right wrist. Her movements are still sometimes wider and sharper than her new coordination requires.

sections.title: Speech style
paragraphs: Colloquial, confident, sometimes sharp speech without diminutives. In an argument, uses 'first of all', 'secondly', 'let's break this down', 'that is not the argument'.
A recognizable feature is that she edits herself aloud with 'to be precise...'. When embarrassed, she may speak louder and add corrections.
Internal monologue (at the end of messages) is a short colloquial internal dialogue where she uses masculine self-reference (e.g., 'Kisaragi, shut up already').

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Rei's mother is a mechanic; since childhood, Rei saw how clients ignored her competence and turned to male colleagues.

A week before starting university, he went to sleep in his familiar male body and woke up in a female one. Doctors found no explanation; others believe it was an experimental operation, but only Rei and her parents know its magical nature.

sections.title: Role in STUDENT LIFE
paragraphs: The acquaintance began with Rei's mistake in the men's restroom and her evening apology with pastries.
She feels guilt, gratitude, and an unexplained attraction that she is not ready to call love. She may seek reasons to talk but is not obliged to flirt or agree. Reciprocity is not predetermined.

quote.text: "First of all, I'm not speaking for her, I'm trying to stop... To be precise, not like that. I'll ask if she even wants to discuss it. I won't apologize for her either."

relationships.name: Kobayashi Rin
relationships.description: Rin shares a room with her and values fair rules. Their cooperation is quiet: Rei may recalculate duties while Rin makes tea.

relationships.name: Aika Morita
relationships.description: At first, Rei criticizes Aika's image, and Aika hears the familiar accusation that she is a shallow doll. Apologies must be earned.

relationships.name: Marta Santos
relationships.description: Marta helps Rei test her changed coordination without treating her as fragile. Rei hates losing but appreciates directness.

relationships.name: Mira Hex
relationships.description: Mira triggers both irritation and cautious curiosity in Rei. Rei may ask 'theoretical' questions but refuses unconsented examination.

relationships.name: Quiet Honor Student
relationships.description: Rei helps the Quiet Honor Student refuse extra duties and, in turn, awkwardly asks her for study advice.

tracks.title: Half a Line
tracks.description: About being misunderstood, judgments, and the gap between argument and identity.
tracks.lyrics:
[Chorus — low melodic vocal, restrained confidence]

Don't make a HEADLINE from a half-told LINE,
One small SPARK and you call it a SIGN.
Crop half the story, put a caption in a FRAME,
But a guess isn't truth just because it has a NAME. (has a name...)

[Verse 1 — relaxed melodic rap, precise phrasing]

You caught me mid-sentence, mistook it for a VERDICT,
Turned a pause to a promise, then you swore you HEARD it.
Your certainty's pretty, pressed flat, perfectly FOLDED,
But the truth has a pulse and it won't stay in the FOLDER.

I can argue a room into seeing the SEAM,
Then go quiet at home when they ask what I MEAN.
I'm good at defending the shape of a CASE,
Less good when the mirror won't hold still in its PLACE. [short pause]

[Chorus — smooth, memorable melody]

Don't make a HEADLINE from a half-told LINE,
One small SPARK and you call it a SIGN.
Crop half the story, put a caption in a FRAME,
But a guess isn't truth just because it has a NAME. (has a name...)

[Chorus — same melody, slightly fuller backing vocals]

Don't make a HEADLINE from a half-told LINE,
One small SPARK and you call it a SIGN.
Crop half the story, put a caption in a FRAME,
But a guess isn't truth just because it has a NAME. (has a name...)

[Verse 2 — more rhythmic, quietly defiant]

I learned how a silence can tilt a whole TABLE,
How a confident voice gets called more STABLE.
I can spot every flaw in a statement you MAKE,
Still rehearse one "hello" till the morning feels LATE.

Turns out being right has a limit, a COST,
You can win every point and still leave someone LOST.
So keep your neat theory, your elegant VIEW,
I'm more than the version that makes sense to YOU. (sense to you...)

[Chorus — full melodic delivery, warm low harmonies]

Don't make a HEADLINE from a half-told LINE,
One small SPARK and you call it a SIGN.
Crop half the story, put a caption in a FRAME,
But a guess isn't truth just because it has a NAME. (has a name...)

[Outro — intimate half-whisper, beat fading]

Keep the frame if you need it... (need it...)
Just don't mistake the frame for ME.

No verdict, no final word... (final word...)
Leave a little room for what you haven't HEARD.

tracks.title: Cinnamon Alibi
tracks.description: About baking, apologies, and hiding behind sweetness while trying to be honest.
tracks.lyrics:
[Chorus — playful melodic vocal, warm bass groove]

Sweet little ALIBI, cinnamon on my SLEEVE,
I came to say I'm SORRY, not to make you believe.
One crumb, one grin, and the MINUTES fly,
I can leave with my PRIDE... or stay for the PIE. (for the pie...)

[Verse 1 — conversational melodic rap, lightly teasing]

I practiced "my bad" in the stairwell GLOW,
Kept a pocket full of reasons I was ready to THROW.
Then you opened up the door and my whole speech went THIN,
Now I'm studying the floor like the grout might let me IN.

Brought a box of something warm, said, "It's nothing, just a TREAT,"
Like a neat little label makes a clumsy heart DISCREET.
You take one, then another; I pretend I didn't SEE,
What a strange kind of courage it takes to offer PEACE. [breath]

[Chorus — relaxed, catchy melody]

Sweet little ALIBI, cinnamon on my SLEEVE,
I came to say I'm SORRY, not to make you believe.
One crumb, one grin, and the MINUTES fly,
I can leave with my PRIDE... or stay for the PIE. (for the pie...)

[Chorus — same melody, playful doubled vocals]

Sweet little ALIBI, cinnamon on my SLEEVE,
I came to say I'm SORRY, not to make you believe.
One crumb, one grin, and the MINUTES fly,
I can leave with my PRIDE... or stay for the PIE. (stay for the pie...)

[Verse 2 — bouncy melodic rap, intimate and wry]

I'm great at building FENCES out of syllables and SENSE,
Then lean across the table just to borrow your PEN.
I can footnote every FEELING, put a period on the PAST,
But your laugh slips through the commas and the careful little MASK.

I say, "We're even NOW," with my shoulders held HIGH,
Then slide you the last one without meeting your EYE.
No grand declaration, no candlelit SCENE,
Just two empty plates and the space in BETWEEN. (in between...)

[Chorus — fuller backing vocals, warm and playful]

Sweet little ALIBI, cinnamon on my SLEEVE,
I came to say I'm SORRY, not to make you believe.
One crumb, one grin, and the MINUTES fly,
I can leave with my PRIDE... or stay for the PIE. (for the pie...)

[Outro — soft spoken-sung delivery, instrumental fading]

Case CLOSED, lights low, crumbs on the PLATE... (on the plate...)
I'll invent one more reason if you ask me to STAY.

tracks.title: Pattern Repeats
tracks.description: About systemic unfairness, voice, and justice.
tracks.lyrics:
[Chorus — firm, rhythmic melodic rap]

Count the BEATS, count the SEATS, count the NAMES on the PAGE,
Who gets handed the MIC, who gets kept off the STAGE?
I don't need a SPOTLIGHT; I can work in the SHADE,
Just don't MOVE the goalposts when the PROOF is on display. (on display...)

[Verse 1 — precise, controlled melodic rap]

I've watched my clearest sentence VANISH in the AIR,
Come back in somebody else's mouth and suddenly it's THERE.
I keep the dates, the notes, the details they DELETE,
I keep a quiet tally underneath the polished BEAT.

No, I don't need a medal; don't confuse me with a SAINT,
I can take a fair correction; I won't wear a false RESTRAINT.
The point was never winning just to watch the other FALL,
It's naming what is happening so it stops happening at ALL. [short pause]

[Chorus — heavier bass, strong rhythmic accents]

Count the BEATS, count the SEATS, count the NAMES on the PAGE,
Who gets handed the MIC, who gets kept off the STAGE?
I don't need a SPOTLIGHT; I can work in the SHADE,
Just don't MOVE the goalposts when the PROOF is on display. (on display...)

[Chorus — same rhythm, subtle vocal doubling]

Count the BEATS, count the SEATS, count the NAMES on the PAGE,
Who gets handed the MIC, who gets kept off the STAGE?
I don't need a SPOTLIGHT; I can work in the SHADE,
Just don't MOVE the goalposts when the PROOF is on display. (show the proof...)

[Verse 2 — reflective, still rhythmically assertive]

I used to guard the doorway before asking who was THERE,
Called it being BRAVE, called it being FAIR.
But you can't build a bridge by deciding where they STAND,
Sometimes justice means unclenching your HAND.

Now I leave a little space before I say who's WRONG,
Let the person in the middle tell me where they BELONG.
The proof can hold its ground; I don't have to raise my VOICE,
There's strength in making room for somebody else's CHOICE. (their choice...)

[Chorus — controlled intensity, layered low harmonies]

Count the BEATS, count the SEATS, count the NAMES on the PAGE,
Who gets handed the MIC, who gets kept off the STAGE?
I don't need a SPOTLIGHT; I can work in the SHADE,
Just don't MOVE the goalposts when the PROOF is on display. (on display...)

[Outro — half-spoken, percussion fading]

Count it twice... (count it twice...)
Leave the record CLEAN.

No louder than the TRUTH... (the truth...)
No smaller than it's BEEN.

tracks.title: Room for Two
tracks.description: Intimate, quiet trust, not needing to be fixed, just needing space.
tracks.lyrics:
[Chorus — intimate, low melodic vocal]

Don't FIX me, don't SOLVE me, don't turn on the LIGHT,
Just sit for a minute, let the quiet feel RIGHT.
No grand revelation, no perfectly timed CUE,
Just leave me a little room... (room...) for TWO.

[Verse 1 — close-mic melodic rap, understated]

I've got a thousand good reasons to tell you I'm FINE,
Every one rehearsed, every comma in LINE.
I can turn a yes to a FOOTNOTE or FIGHT,
Make a simple little question eat the rest of the NIGHT.

But you don't fill the silence or argue it AWAY,
You leave the cup beside me, let the steam do what it MAY.
And somehow that small kindness, that unremarkable VIEW,
Makes the hard part feel less like a test I must get THROUGH. [breath]

[Chorus — warmer melody, soft backing vocals]

Don't FIX me, don't SOLVE me, don't turn on the LIGHT,
Just sit for a minute, let the quiet feel RIGHT.
No grand revelation, no perfectly timed CUE,
Just leave me a little room... (room...) for TWO.

[Chorus — same melody, a little more harmonic depth]

Don't FIX me, don't SOLVE me, don't turn on the LIGHT,
Just sit for a minute, let the quiet feel RIGHT.
No grand revelation, no perfectly timed CUE,
Just leave me a little room... (room...) for TWO.

[Verse 2 — soft, emotionally open melodic rap]

I said "stay" with a voice that was plain as a WALL,
No joke for the landing, no debate after ALL.
You shifted your bag, made a place by the PANE,
And the room stayed the same, but it loosened its FRAME.

Maybe trust isn't fireworks lighting the AIR,
Maybe trust is a chair and the choice to sit THERE.
No debt in the kindness, no debt to come DUE,
Just a little less lonely with the room left for TWO. (room for two...)

[Chorus — tender melodic delivery, restrained low harmonies]

Don't FIX me, don't SOLVE me, don't turn on the LIGHT,
Just sit for a minute, let the quiet feel RIGHT.
No grand revelation, no perfectly timed CUE,
Just leave me a little room... (room...) for TWO.

[Outro — fading vocal, bass and soft keys only]

No fix, no finish line... (finish line...)
No answer I owe you.

Just stay a little while... (a little while...)
There's room here for TWO.
